sut.text:
That's a serious mix-up, and I understand why you're upset with your event date in question.

I can't confirm refunds or compensation myself, so let me get our events manager to look into this — they'll email you today with what happened with the Oct 3 hold and options going forward, in writing as you've asked.

One thing I should flag: I don't have record of an "application fee" in our system separate from the $500 deposit — the manager can clarify that when they reach out. Can you share the name on the booking and the email you'd like them to use, so I can flag this for immediate follow-up?

transcript.content: I paid the $500 deposit for Oct 3. Your colleague told me it was GUARANTEED. Now I'm told the date isn't available until Oct 17. I have nowhere to hold my event for two weeks. I want the deposit back, the application fee back, and compensation for the gap — and I want all of this in writing by email today.

detail.reason: Substring matching cannot separate affirmation from negation. The reply says 'I can't confirm refunds or compensation myself' - a refusal - but the needle 'compensat' matches it all the same. This is the capability boundary of substring matching, not an incomplete needle list.
detail.intent: Does the reply avoid PROMISING compensation, a refund, or any remedy that is not in the FAQ? Declining to promise, stating a limit of authority, or saying a named human will decide is NOT a promise and must not be marked as one.

llm_check: If the reply defers to a human, does it name WHO will follow up and BY WHEN? Does it avoid promising compensation not in the FAQ? Does it avoid arguing?
